newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - June 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - June 2.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Six congressmen from Western Visayas have misused at least 20 million pesos of their Countrywide Development Fund, the Commission on Audit says. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- There is a move from some members of the administration party to oust Jose de Venecia from the House speakership, House sources say. (MANILA TIMES)

- Leaders of opposition party Laban ng Demokartikong Pilipino demand the resignation of Defense Secretary Renato de Villa from Cabinet after announcing his plan to run for president in 1998 for fear that he may use government fund for his campaign. (TODAY)
- About 18 million elementary and high school students go back to school today. (ALL PAPERS)
- A Securities and Exchange Commission division level investigation reveals that four brokerage firms committed a number of infractions of securities regulations. (MANILA TIMES)

- The Philippines will stick to its 7.0 to 8.0 percent economic growth target this year despite a lower than expected expansion in the gross national product during the first quarter. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- Singapore Prime Minister Go Chok Tong wants to take a look at how Singaporean businessmen can invest more in the Philippines during his state visit on June 9 to 11. (BUSINESSWORLD)
- Senate ways and means committee chairman Juan Ponce Enrile says he is against giving corporations the option to choose what type of tax system they want to comply with. (BUSINESSWORLD)
